title: The Diamond PAU replaces the monolithic controller with a facet-dispatch architecture whose facets are shared across Agents
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.4 defines the newer of Grove's two execution architectures: "The Diamond PAU is a modular implementation of the Allocation System in which the Controller dispatches operations to shared Facet contracts, with integration configurations held in a shared Beacon contract. The Beacon and the Facet contracts are shared across Diamond PAU implementations and are specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.3 - Liquidity Layer Shared Contracts]."

The contrast with the "monolithic ALM Controller" (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.1.1.1) is the point. A monolith must contain code for every protocol it integrates, so adding an integration means upgrading the controller that already custodies live positions. The Diamond pattern moves each integration into its own facet and leaves the Controller as a dispatcher, so a new integration is a new facet rather than a modification to the hot path.

What makes this an *ecosystem* decision rather than an engineering one is the word **shared**. The facets and the Beacon are not Grove's — they are defined in the Sky Core Atlas and shared across every Agent's Diamond PAU. Integration code is therefore written, audited and fixed once for the whole ecosystem, which is the contract-level counterpart of the document-level inheritance in A.6.1.1.2.2.5.1.2.1.2.1.

The trade-off is the same as with document inheritance, transposed to code. Grove gains audited integrations it did not have to build, and accepts that a bug in a shared facet is a bug in every Agent simultaneously, and that its execution surface can change without any Grove-specific deployment. The Beacon holding "integration configurations" that the Controller "synchronizes" means Grove's live behaviour tracks an external contract's state.
description: A Controller synchronizes integration configurations from a shared Beacon contract and dispatches to shared Facet contracts specified in the Sky Core Atlas, so integration code is written once
